ops.title: FP backend SHIPPED v0.39.0 (2026-07-04): fleet on fileprovider domains; hard-won macOS platform facts — Settings toggle + one-time daemon TCC prompt, sandbox AF_UNIX rules, FPFS size-0 short-circuit, appex persists priv
ops.body:
**cc-pool v0.39.0 (2026-07-04): the macOS File Provider backend is LIVE** — 9 accounts on
`fileprovider` domains, pool default flipped; acct-06/11/12 pending session-end migration
(`ccp migrate --account N --to fileprovider`; doctor nags via checkFileProviderFallback). No
fuse mounts remain; the holder/mux path stays for any future fuse rows (cask 0.29.0 on disk).
fusekit needed one fix: **v0.29.1** mux Teardown legacy per-dir arm (real-dir rows tear down via
the pre-mux path — without it no legacy row could ever escape fuse).

Platform facts that cost hours — trust these:
1. **Two separate enablement gates**: `pluginkit -e use` ('+' election) satisfies
   FileProviderAvailable, but fileproviderd separately holds the provider "⏹ user-disabled"
   (visible in `fileproviderctl dump <bundle-id>`) until the System Settings ▸ Login Items &
   Extensions ▸ File Providers toggle is flipped. No API/CLI flips it (cc-notes f8e89e7 tracks
   the UX guidance).
2. **The daemon's first bind in the App Group container blocks on a one-time TCC GUI prompt**
   (macOS 15+ group-container protection; entitled Developer ID CLI still prompts once). The
   bind HANGS silently until the user approves — looks like a wedge. Approve once, permanent.
   The FP bridge serve loop retries with backoff + logs real errors precisely for this.
3. **Sandboxed appex AF_UNIX rules**: file temp-exceptions (home-relative-path.read-write) do
   NOT cover connect(2) (network-outbound op); `network.client` covers REMOTE endpoints only —
   also insufficient. The group container is the only sanctioned socket location for
   appex↔daemon UDS. (Loopback TCP + token file was the fallback design, never needed.)
4. **FPFS satisfies a size-0 read WITHOUT calling fetchContents** — computed items must
   advertise their real byte length (appex does a bridge read per freshness-version, cached,
   "sz1:" version salt) or merged .claude.json/settings.json materialize EMPTY.
5. **The appex persists a committed .claude.json to the private backing itself** (mirrors the
   fuse holder's division of labor; Go WriteThrough only splits shareables to base). Without it
   private-key changes silently vanish on the next merge.
6. **Split has no deletion semantics**: removing a key through a domain write does not delete
   it from ~/.claude.json — clean base directly if needed.
7. fileproviderd redacts extension errors ("FP -1004 <private>"); the appex NSLogs enumeration
   failures (search `ccp-fp` in unified log). Poisoned domain enumeration state survives bridge
   recovery — re-register the domain (remove+register via ~/.cc-pool/domains.sock) to reset.
8. **Recovery goldmine**: every account keeps claude's own config backups at
   `acct-NN.private/backups/.claude.json.backup.*` (dotfiles — ls -a!). Restoring the newest
   into priv + signalEnumerator resurrects a stubbed account. Used to recover 6 accounts after
   the [[holder-bg-band-incident]] holder crash.

Cert/signing: Developer ID imported from 1Password OpenClaw (Stage 0); local FP builds signed
with team SXKCTF23Q2, `security import -T /usr/bin/codesign` avoided partition-list prompts.
Related: [[fusekit-content-over-rpc]], [[cc-pool-fileprovider-signing-reality]],
[[claude-pool-project]].
